scope.support: s. 19(a) הכנסת רשאית, ברוב של חבריה, להביע אי-אמון לראש הממשלה; s. 27(a) removal by eighty members; s. 35(c) removal of a minister by seventy.
scope.note: Checks are reconfigured, not removed: no confidence now needs a majority of members and entails dissolution of the Knesset (s. 19(b), s. 21), and the prime minister may dissolve the Knesset with the President's consent (s. 22), but both trigger elections for Knesset and prime minister together; the Knesset keeps approval of the government's composition (s. 3(c)), removal of the prime minister (ss. 26-27) and of ministers (s. 35(c)), control of penal regulations (s. 48), information and attendance powers (s. 52), and declaration and revocation of emergencies (s. 49). Emergency regulations may alter any law (s. 50(c)) but are bounded (s. 50(d)-(f), s. 53). The 100-day cooling-off for judges, dayanim and career officers in the 1968 law's s. 5(b) is dropped (s. 16(a)), a relaxation but not the removal of a check; s. 25 channels criminal process against the prime minister through the Attorney-General and a three-judge Jerusalem District Court panel without immunising him. No protected right is removed.

temporary_provision.support: Permanent re-enactment replacing Basic Law: The Government 1968 (s. 61: חוק-יסוד: הממשלה — בטל); s. 64 transitional only.

targets_judiciary.support: Subject: election, formation, powers and accountability of the government (ss. 1-55).
targets_judiciary.note: Judicial provisions are incidental: s. 25 (prime minister investigated only with the Attorney-General's consent and tried by a three-judge Jerusalem District Court panel), s. 42 (ministers may not assume powers of a judicial character), s. 50(d) (emergency regulations may not bar recourse to the courts), s. 16(a) (former judges may become ministers once they have left office), s. 62(6) (election appeals). None makes judicial review, appointments or independence the subject.

deviation_tier.support: s. 57 inserts s. 9A: הכנסת לא תאריך את תקופת כהונתה אלא בחוק שנתקבל ברוב של שמונים חברי הכנסת ואם נתקיימו נסיבות מיוחדות המונעות עריכת בחירות בעיתן.
deviation_tier.note: Principal subject: separation of powers (the executive's source of authority and its relationship with the Knesset: separately elected prime minister, s. 3(b); Knesset approval of ministers, s. 3(c); no confidence by a majority of members with dissolution, ss. 19-21; prime minister's dissolution power with the President's consent, s. 22; removal of the prime minister, ss. 26-27; Knesset removal of ministers, s. 35(c); subordinate legislation and emergency powers under Knesset control, ss. 48-50, 53; oversight duties, s. 52; continuing budget capped at one-twelfth, s. 58; entrenchment, s. 56). Other values engaged, all entrenched: free and equal elections (ss. 3(b), 6, 13, 8(b), 57, 62); rule of law (ss. 17-18, 25, 43, 50(d)-(f), 53); core human rights (s. 50(d)); an independent judiciary (ss. 50(d), 42). Contradicts none sharply. Provisions that cut the other way and on which another reader might code Limited (separation of powers): the no-confidence check made costlier (s. 19(b)), the executive's new dissolution power (s. 22), the removal of the judges'/officers' cooling-off (s. 16(a)), Attorney-General gatekeeping of investigations of the prime minister (s. 25(a)), and government secrecy (s. 44); coded as a reconfiguration of mutual checks rather than a contradiction.

direction.support: s. 50(d): אין בכוחן של תקנות שעת-חירום למנוע פניה לערכאות, לקבוע ענישה למפרע, או להתיר פגיעה בכבוד האדם.
direction.note: Coded from the principal subject (electoral and institutional reconstruction of the executive). Axes engaged: judicial review/independence, mildly in the liberal direction (s. 50(d), s. 42, s. 53) and very mildly the other way (s. 16(a) drops the cooling-off before a judge may become a minister); Jewish identity versus equal citizenship: not engaged (the only reference is the ballot slip printed in Hebrew or Hebrew and Arabic, s. 62(10)); rights of minorities or women: not engaged.
